transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25
Start: 09:00 PST
Duration: 53m
Attendees: Lina Martinez (Redwood AE), Marco Tan (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Redwood CSM); Priya Rao (Catalyst Head of ML), Samir Gupta (Platform), Olivia Chen (Security), Ben Hall (SRE)

Summary:
Quick sync to validate canary signals, finalize go/no-go matrix for pilot cutover, and agree rollback/traffic fallback runbook. Shared deck and telemetry links referenced.

Topics:
- Canary signal thresholds and what "green" looks like
- A/B routing decision rules and traffic steering fallback
- Rollback playbook and automated vs manual gates
- KV cache warming and cold-starts during traffic shift
- Security/crypto sign-offs (KMS, audit logs)

Action items (captured verbally, also in metadata): see action_items field.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lina Martinez: okay, thanks everyone for hopping on. quick agenda — canary signals, go/no-go matrix, rollback playbook. we'll keep this tight, 45 max but looks like 53 today, sorry.
[00:22] Priya Rao: yeah that's fine. we ran the pilot load tests overnight — some results to share. there were, uh, a couple of tail latency spikes when sequence lengths hit longer prompts.
[00:32] Marco Tan: can you — sorry to interrupt — what GPU instance did you route to in that test? was that Redwood Dedicated or the hosted cluster?
[00:40] Priya Rao: we started on hosted, then retargeted to Dedicated reserved pool for the second run. the Dedicated run had fewer spikes but still two outliers at 95th.
[00:52] Samir Gupta: and those outliers correlated with cache misses, I think the KV cache was cold for some customer-side prompts. we didn't prime it.
[01:05] Marco Tan: right, KV cache priming is critical. for the cutover we recommend a 24-hour warmup with synthetic prefixes that match real traffic. that usually eliminates the cold-kv spikes.
[01:18] Ben Hall: question on that — if we do a 24 hour warmup, what's the cost estimate? we need to include that in our go/no-go calculation.
[01:28] Lina Martinez: good point. we'll add estimated token and instance hours to the matrix. Marco, can you give a ballpark?
[01:33] Marco Tan: ballpark, for your pilot scale (approx 3k qps peak) warmup is roughly 12-18 GPU-hours across the Dedicated pool; i'll put exact in the doc.
[01:42] Priya Rao: ok. next, signal thresholds — we suggested 95th p99 latency, error rate less than 0.5%, and hallucination rate under our eval baseline.
[01:52] Olivia Chen: about hallucination metric — that's fuzzier. our legal team asked for guardrails if hallucination causes PHI exposure, obviously non-starter. do you have rollback hooks tied to content filters?
[02:04] Marco Tan: yes, we can wire content-filter triggers into the rollback automation. if a X number of flagged responses happen in a 5-minute window, traffic will divert to a conservative model variant and raise an alert. note: transcription may spell the product as 'Red-would' sometimes in logs but it's the same.
[02:22] Priya Rao: okay can you define 'conservative variant'? is that smaller context or quantized?
[02:28] Marco Tan: it's a model variant we pre-compile with stricter decoding and higher temperature clamp — lower creativity. also optionally a variant running in 8-bit quant that reduces cost but is less liberal.
[02:39] Lina Martinez: let's make that explicit in the matrix: if hallucination spike > threshold then route 20% to conservative, 80% keep, then escalate to 100% if persists 15 minutes.
[02:51] Samir Gupta: for A/B we need the traffic split rules. currently we planned a 5% canary for 6 hours, then 25% for 18 hours, then decision. do we want SLO gates in place for each step?
[03:03] Marco Tan: absolutely, each step has SLO gates — key SLOs: p95 latency < 600ms, error rate < 0.5%, model-quality delta < 2% on eval set. if any gate trips, rollback to previous stable.
[03:15] Ben Hall: how are SLOs computed in the console? we want token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards.
[03:21] Asha Patel: Redwood Console exposes per-route latency and token cost, and you can wire alerts into PagerDuty. Marco will add the exact dashboard link to the doc.
[03:30] Priya Rao: we'd like to automate the go/no-go matrix evaluation as much as possible — manual decisions are slow. what's the automation surface?
[03:39] Marco Tan: you can define automated gates in the rollout configuration: thresholds, evaluation window, and auto-rollback actions. we support canary->A/B funnels and automated fallback to model variants or a different region.
[03:50] Olivia Chen: on region failover — we need to ensure data residency. if the fallback region is outside our EU boundary, that's a deal-breaker. can the routing policy respect region constraints?
[03:59] Marco Tan: yes, routing policies can be region-aware. for your EU traffic we can pin to EU hosts and only failover within EU capacity tiers. we'll document that.
[04:10] Priya Rao: good. on observability: Marco you mentioned adding synthetic canaries — do those live run through the same inference path (including caching)?
[04:19] Marco Tan: they do. we run synthetic probes that hit the same endpoints so they exercise the cache and KV hits just like real traffic.
[04:26] Samir Gupta: about rollback playbook — what are the manual steps vs automated? we need a concise checklist for on-call.
[04:34] Lina Martinez: here's the draft playbook: 1) detect gate failure (auto alert), 2) determine scope (model only, routing, infra), 3) hit fast rollback (1-click rollback to previous model), 4) if rollback fails, divert to conservative model variant, 5) escalate to SRE and SE, 6) run postmortem. we'll attach runbook links.
[04:52] Ben Hall: what is '1-click' rollback? is that immediate or queued?
[04:56] Marco Tan: immediate if automation is enabled — it flips the routing to the previous model version and rebalances traffic. there's a safety window configurable to require manual approve.
[05:05] Priya Rao: can we add a freeze window for high-risk times? like no cutovers during Monday 8-11am for us.
[05:11] Lina Martinez: yes we'll encode freeze windows into the rollout policy.
[05:15] Samir Gupta: also we saw a couple of misattributions in the transcript from last demo — "Rudewood" vs Redwood etc. hope the tooling gets better.
[05:23] Marco Tan: noted, fireflies transcriptions sometimes mangle names.
[05:27] Priya Rao: let's talk about thresholds numerically — for this pilot we propose: p95 < 450ms, p99 < 900ms, error rate < 0.3%, model-quality delta < 1.5%. are those acceptable?
[05:40] Marco Tan: p95 is achievable if you accept slightly higher cost; if you need p95 < 300ms we suggest more aggressive batching or larger Dedicated pool.
[05:49] Priya Rao: cost tradeoff is a factor. Samir, finance needs a quick estimate for the warmup and higher SLOs.
[05:57] Samir Gupta: we'll run the cost calc after Marco shares the instance-hour estimate.
[06:02] Lina Martinez: action: Marco add cost table to doc.
[06:06] Marco Tan: done.
[06:09] Olivia Chen: security items — audit logs retention, SSO SAML integration, and KMS key rotation cadence. we need those documented and ideally a runbook for a key rotation during pilot.
[06:21] Asha Patel: Redwood supports KMS integration; rotation is customer-controlled. we'll include rotation steps and an example schedule.
[06:29] Priya Rao: can we schedule a short security deep-dive next week to close open questions?
[06:34] Lina Martinez: yes — let's target 2026-03-02 for a 30-minute security review. Olivia will confirm.
[06:41] Olivia Chen: sounds good.
[06:44] Samir Gupta: on telemetry we saw a drift in latency coinciding with a change in prompt length distribution around 2 AM in the logs. our plan is to add distribution-aware routing that auto-scales kernel selection. does Redwood runtime support that?
[06:58] Marco Tan: yes, runtime does kernel selection per-sequence-length and we can tune compilation choices. there is a small warmup when a new kernel path is used. we'll document recommended sequence-length buckets.
[07:10] Priya Rao: what's the plan for A/B evaluation on model-quality? do we compute per-candidate BLEU-style metrics or use our eval harness?
[07:18] Marco Tan: we can ingest your eval harness results and compute deltas. we also support per-prompt scoring hooks so you can score live samples with your metric.
[07:27] Ben Hall: are live-sample scoring hooks impacting latency? we can't add SLO noise.
[07:32] Marco Tan: scoring hooks are asynchronous by default; they don't block response path unless you configure sync scoring.
[07:38] Priya Rao: good. ok, let's run through the proposed go/no-go matrix now — Lina, you want to share the quick screen? (screen-share note: deck link: https://redwood.docs/pilot-gonogo — referenced)
[07:52] Lina Martinez: reading out the matrix: Step 0: preflight — infra and security sign-off. Step 1: canary 5% for 6h — SLO gates p95,p99,error,quality. Step 2: ramp to 25% for 18h — same gates. Step 3: 100% after 48h green or manual sign-off. each gate requires no more than 2 failing metrics to proceed.
[08:20] Priya Rao: i want a single-line go/no-go green criteria for exec: e.g., 'no SLO breaches, no security flags, and <2% quality regression' — can we write that?
[08:33] Lina Martinez: yes, we will include an exec summary one-liner.
[08:36] Samir Gupta: what about partial rollbacks? say we see token-level cost spike but quality is ok — do we roll back or throttle?
[08:45] Marco Tan: you can throttle by adjusting concurrency or shifting percent to cheaper model variants. rollback should be for quality/regressions or safety issues. cost adjustments are usually handled by autoscaling or throttles.
[08:56] Priya Rao: okay. final topic: communications and on-call. who pagers on SLO breach?
[09:03] Ben Hall: SRE owns infra, SE gets paged for model-quality, and Redwood CSM gets included for customer comms. let's list exact escalation paths in doc.
[09:15] Lina Martinez: agreed. we'll produce a one-page cheat sheet for on-call and exec stakeholders.
[09:21] Priya Rao: great. thanks all. any other Qs?
[09:25] Olivia Chen: quick ask — include sample audit log entry format so our auditors can validate fields.
[09:31] Asha Patel: will do.
[09:33] Priya Rao: ok wrapping — recap and next steps? Lina?
[09:36] Lina Martinez: recap: share go/no-go matrix and rollback playbook (Lina), Marco to add cost and telemetry dashboard links and SLO gate definitions, Samir to run synthetic warmup and share logs, Olivia to schedule security deep-dive. check the metadata for due dates.
[09:49] Priya Rao: thanks, see you next week.
